slides.title: In-person habits do not transfer
slides.intro: The same agenda that works in a meeting room often collapses online.

slides.title: What is a workshop?
slides.definition: A structured working session in which a group actively produces a concrete outcome together, rather than receiving information passively.
notes: The outcome — a decision, a plan, a prototype — is agreed before the session starts
If participants could be replaced by an email, it is a meeting, not a workshop

columns.heading: Participation
columns.body: Every attendee contributes something visible in the first ten minutes.

columns.heading: Rhythm
columns.body: Alternate intensity: never more than fifteen minutes in one mode.

columns.heading: Clarity
columns.body: At any moment everyone knows what is being asked of them.

slides.title: Key takeaway
slides.statement: A remote workshop succeeds by design, not by chance — structure participation, protect the rhythm, and make every instruction impossible to misunderstand.
points: Change the mode every fifteen minutes
